newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel issues tender for $700 mln toll highway.
newsitem.headline: Israel issues tender for $700 mln toll highway.

text.p: Israel's Trans-Israel Highway Co has issued a closed tender to four consortia for the construction of the main segment of the highway, a company spokesman said on Monday.
The main segment is 90 km (60 mile) long and runs between Hadera in the north and Gedera in the south. The cost of the segment is estimated at $700 million.

The consortia consist of Israeli and foreign companies, including Transroute International of France, Atkinson of the United States; Holzmann of Germany, Parsons Brinckerhoff of the United States, Autostrada of Italy, Bouygues of France, Canadian Highways, Hughes Aircraft Co (part of General Motors), Dragados y Construcciones SA of Spain and Britain's Tarmac Construction.
"The four groups have six months to submit their documents and then we expect to award the project by the end of 1997," the spokesman said.
The consortium that wins the tender will build and operate the highway for 30 years.
The Trans-Israel Highway is due to run from Rosh Hanikra, on Israel's northern border with Lebanon, to a point south of Beersheba. It will be the country's first toll road.
Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu said the main aim of the higway is to attract major portions of the population and industry to Israel's hinterland.
